note: The Falkland Islands, read on Falkland Islands Legislation (legislation.gov.fk, the Falkland Islands Government's in-force texts, as at 31 October 2026), 2026-10-31. Majority: the Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance 1977, s. 3: the age of majority is eighteen, and an infant or minor is a person under eighteen. Emancipation by marriage isn't held. Work: the Employment of Children Ordinance 1966 (as revised; s. 3 as amended by Ord. 3/2006 from 30 March 2006) calls a child anyone under, or still of, compulsory school age, and bars employing a child under 14, and any child before the close of school hours, before 7 a.m. or after 7 p.m., for more than two hours on a school day or a Sunday, or in harmful work; so 14 is the youngest age a person may be employed, with those limits until the end of compulsory schooling (not held). The Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Ordinance 1967 adds limits for industrial work, not read in full. Performers: the 1966 Ordinance makes no exception for performing (only a chorister in a religious service is deemed not employed, and babysitting from 14 is free of the limits), so performers under 14 are barred (my reading). Service: the Falkland Islands Defence Force Ordinance 1991 has the Force of members who enlist (active and reserve, from 17 to 55, women as men, British subjects only) and no standing emergency reserve: residents of 17 to 55 become liable only when the Governor musters them by proclamation in an emergency (ss. 6, 54); so service is none, the emergency muster not held.
